about: The clauses, inferences and spec conflicts the KERI cases cite, from the KERI specification v1.0.1 (tag v1.0.1, commit 71cb54ebb445dd9d8cb33cd29a5f50894fafc569, spec/spec-body.md). Each quote must appear verbatim exactly once in the pinned text, under the named heading; a clause's quote must contain its level's keyword. The generator checks all of this before it writes a case.

accept-precondition.quote: Given a local or remote event, a non-controller, non-witness, non-delegator validator MUST first verify the event's controller signatures, witness signatures (if witnessed), and delegator anchoring seal (if delegated) before it can accept that event into its copy of that event's KEL.

act-as-verifier.quote: Therefore, a validator MUST first act as a verifier in order to establish the root authoritative set of keys and verify the associated signatures.

backer-threshold.quote: This is the number of backers in the backer list that MUST support a key event for it to be valid.

backer-unique.quote: A given AID MUST NOT appear more than once in any Backer list.

controlling-keys.quote: In order to verify signatures, a verifier MUST first determine which set of keys are or were the controlling set for the AID of that event when the event was issued.

delegation-seal.quote: A [[ref: Validator]] MUST be given or find the delegating seal in the delegator’s KEL before the event may be accepted as valid.

dnd-drop.quote: A Validator MUST invalidate, i.e., drop any delegated events whose Delegator has this configuration trait.

drop-unsigned.quote: A [[ref: Validator]] that receives a key event or non-key-event message that does not have attached at least one verifiable Controller signature MUST drop that message (i.e., not escrow or otherwise accept it).

drt-fields.quote: The top-level fields of a Delegated Rotation, `drt` event message body MUST appear in the following order: `[ v, t, d, i, s, p, kt, k, nt, n, bt, br, ba, c, a]`.

eo-drop.quote: A Validator MUST invalidate, i.e., drop any non-establishment events.

escrow-thresholds.quote: Events that have a non-empty set of attached signatures which set does not satisfy the REQUIRED thresholds SHOULD escrow the event while waiting for other signatures to arrive either as attachments to the same [[ref: Version]] of the event or to a receipt of that event (see next section).

exn-fields.quote: The top-level fields of an Exchange, `exn` message body MUST appear in the following order: `[ v, t, d, i, ri, x, p, dt, r, q, a]`.

exn-prior.quote: When the prior `p` field appears in an exchange message, its value MUST be the SAID of the immediately preceding exchange message in that transaction.

exn-x.quote: The [[ref: Exchange Identifier]] SAID, `x` field value MUST be the SAID, `d` field value of the first message in the set of exchange messages that constitute a transaction.

exn-x-empty.quote: When an exchange message is not part of a transaction, the Exchange Identifier, `x` field value, MUST be the empty string.

exn-xip-first.quote: The first message MUST be an Exchange Inception message with type `xip`.

fields-order.quote: The top-level fields of each message type MUST appear in a specific order.

icp-fields.quote: The top-level fields of an Inception, `icp`, event message body MUST appear in the following order: `[ v, t, d, i, s, kt, k, nt, n, bt, b, c, a]`.

inception-d-i.quote: Validation of an Inception event requires examining the `i` field's derivation code and if it is a digest-type then the `d` field MUST be identical otherwise the Inception event is invalid.

ixn-fields.quote: The top-level fields of an Interaction, `ixn` event message body MUST appear in the following order: `[ v, t, d, i, s, p, a]`.

keys-nonempty.quote: The Key, `k` field value MUST NOT be empty.

message-types.quote: A [[ref: Key event message]] types MUST be one of the following `[icp, rot, ixn, dip, drt]`.

no-events-abandoned.quote: When the Next, `n` field value in a Rotation or Delegated Rotation Event event is an empty list, then the associated AID MUST be deemed abandoned, and no more key events MUST be allowed in its KEL.

no-events-nontransferable.quote: When the Next, `n` field value in an Inception or Delegated Inception event is an empty list, then the associated AID MUST be deemed non-transferable, and no more key events MUST be allowed in that KEL.

nonkey-threshold.quote: A set of controller-indexed signatures on a non-key event message (see below) MUST at least satisfy the signing threshold for the establishment event indicated by the event reference in the attachment group (which MAY or MAY NOT be the current signing threshold) to be accepted as valid.

one-kel.quote: In KERI, there MUST be at most one valid KEL for any identifier or none at all.

prerotation.quote: A Validator, therefore, MUST confirm that the set of keys in the current key list truly includes a satisfiable subset of the prior next key list and that the current key list is satisfiable with respect to both the current and [[xref: keri1, prio-next-threshold, prior next threshold]]s.

rot-fields.quote: The top-level fields of a Rotation, `rot` event message body MUST appear in the following order: `[ v, t, d, i, s, p, kt, k, nt, n, bt, br, ba, c, a]`.

sig-threshold-icp-ixn.quote: A set of controller-indexed signatures on an interaction or inception event (delegated or not) MUST at least satisfy the current signing threshold in order for that event to be accepted as valid.

sig-threshold-rot.quote: A set of controller-indexed signatures on a rotation event (delegated or not) MUST at least satisfy both the current signing threshold and the prior next rotation threshold in order for that event to be accepted as valid.

sn-inception.quote: The Sequence Number, `s` field value in Inceptions, `icp` and Delegated Inception, `dip` events MUST be `0` (hex encoded 0).

sn-increment.quote: The Sequence number value of all subsequent key events in a KEL MUST be 1 greater than the previous event.

sn-max.quote: The maximum value of a sequence number MUST be `ffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffff` which is the hex encoding of `2^128 - 1 = 340282366920938463463374607431768211455`.

supersede-discard.section: Superseding Rules for Recovery at a given location, SN (sequence number).
supersede-discard.quote: The terminal case of the recursive application of C. will occur at the root KEL, which by definition MUST be non-delegated therefore either A. or B. MUST be satisfied, or else the superseding rotation MUST be discarded.

wit-list-order.quote: The AIDs in the Backer Remove, `br` list MUST be removed before any AIDs in the Backer Add, `ba` list are appended.

wit-threshold.quote: A set of witness-indexed signatures on an interaction, inception, or rotation (delegated or not) for which the effective witness list is not empty MUST satisfy the current witness threshold (of accountable duplicity) for that event to be accepted as valid.

witness-nontransferable.quote: When the Backers are Witnesses, then the AIDs themselves MUST be non-transferable, fully qualified public keys.

xip-fields.quote: The top-level fields of an Exchange Transaction Incept, `xip` message body MUST appear in the following order: `[ v, t, d, u, i, ri, dt, r, q, a]`.

liveness.quote: Given a local or remote event, a non-controller, non-witness, non-delegator validator MUST first verify the event's controller signatures, witness signatures (if witnessed), and delegator anchoring seal (if delegated) before it can accept that event into its copy of that event's KEL.
liveness.inference: The sentence states what a validator must verify before it can accept an event, not that it must accept one that passes. No sentence obliges a validator to accept anything, so that a validator should accept an event that passes every check, and that the event is then on the trunk, is inferred and graded SHOULD (docs/design.md, KERI, What MUST means here).

first-seen.quote: Notably, an event that may not supersede, according to the rules below, another event at the same location cannot be first seen at all by that KEL.
first-seen.inference: With rule A2 ("An interaction event may not supersede any event."), this says a validator should not accept an event that is not a rotation where a different event already lies on the trunk. Neither sentence carries a keyword, so refusing it is graded SHOULD, and the state it leaves is graded at the same level.

recovery.section: Superseding Rules for Recovery at a given location, SN (sequence number).
recovery.quote: A0. Any rotation event may supersede an [[ref: Interaction event]] at the same `sn` where that interaction event is not before any other rotation event.
recovery.inference: Rule A0 uses a lowercase "may". A validator that accepts a rotation A0 permits keeps the displaced interaction and everything after it as seen but off the trunk ("All the already-seen but superseded events in the superseded fork still remain in the KEL"). Accepting the rotation, and the resulting trunk, are graded SHOULD as liveness.

exn-liveness.quote: A set of controller-indexed signatures on a non-key event message (see below) MUST at least satisfy the signing threshold for the establishment event indicated by the event reference in the attachment group (which MAY or MAY NOT be the current signing threshold) to be accepted as valid.
exn-liveness.inference: The sentence states a condition for a non-key-event message to be accepted as valid, not that a validator must accept one that meets it. No sentence obliges a validator to accept an exchange message, so that it should accept one that passes every check is inferred and graded SHOULD, as liveness is in the rest of the KERI layer (docs/design.md, IPEX).

exn-prior-link.quote: When the prior `p` field appears in an exchange message, its value MUST be the SAID of the immediately preceding exchange message in that transaction.
exn-prior-link.inference: The sentence binds the sender, who sets `p`. That a validator should not accept an exchange message whose `p` is not the SAID of the message before it in its transaction is inferred from it and graded SHOULD (docs/design.md, IPEX, step 3).

exn-x-link.quote: The [[ref: Exchange Identifier]] SAID, `x` field value MUST be the SAID, `d` field value of the first message in the set of exchange messages that constitute a transaction.
exn-x-link.inference: The sentence binds the sender, who sets `x`. That a validator should not accept an exchange message whose `x` names a message it holds that is not an exchange inception is inferred from it and graded SHOULD (docs/design.md, IPEX, step 3): whichever transaction the message is read as continuing, its `x` is then not the SAID of that transaction's first message. A message whose `x` names a held exchange inception belongs to that transaction, since `x` "universally uniquely associates" a message with its transaction, so a `p` naming a message of another transaction breaks the prior rule instead.

exn-lone.quote: When an exchange message is not part of a transaction, the Exchange Identifier, `x` field value, MUST be the empty string.
exn-lone.inference: The sentence binds the sender. An exchange message whose `x` names no exchange inception the validator holds is refused under either reading of whether it belongs to a transaction: outside one, this sentence requires `x` to be empty; inside one, the transaction's first message must be an `xip` ("The first message MUST be an Exchange Inception message with type `xip`."), and none with that SAID was delivered. Refusing it is inferred and graded SHOULD (docs/design.md, IPEX).

producer-type.quote: A [[ref: Key event message]] types MUST be one of the following `[icp, rot, ixn, dip, drt]`.
producer-type.inference: The sentence defines the values a key event's type may take; no sentence says what a validator does with a message whose type is none of them. That a validator should not accept such a message is inferred and graded SHOULD (docs/design.md, Principles: an obligation the specification states only for producers is graded SHOULD for validators), and the gap is raised in generators/SPEC-ISSUES.md (K-I5).

producer-sn-inception.quote: The Sequence Number, `s` field value in Inceptions, `icp` and Delegated Inception, `dip` events MUST be `0` (hex encoded 0).
producer-sn-inception.inference: The sentence defines the value an inception's sequence number must have; no validator-facing sentence names it. That a validator should not accept an inception with a nonzero sequence number is inferred and graded SHOULD (docs/design.md, Principles: an obligation the specification states only for producers is graded SHOULD for validators), and the gap is raised in generators/SPEC-ISSUES.md (K-I5).

producer-sn-increment.quote: The Sequence number value of all subsequent key events in a KEL MUST be 1 greater than the previous event.
producer-sn-increment.inference: The sentence defines how a later event's sequence number relates to its prior; no validator-facing sentence names a later event at sequence number 0. That a validator should not accept one is inferred and graded SHOULD (docs/design.md, Principles: an obligation the specification states only for producers is graded SHOULD for validators), and the gap is raised in generators/SPEC-ISSUES.md (K-I5).

producer-sn-max.quote: The maximum value of a sequence number MUST be `ffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffff` which is the hex encoding of `2^128 - 1 = 340282366920938463463374607431768211455`.
producer-sn-max.inference: The sentence bounds the value of a sequence number; no sentence says what a validator does with a larger one. That a validator should not accept an event whose sequence number exceeds the maximum is inferred and graded SHOULD (docs/design.md, Principles: an obligation the specification states only for producers is graded SHOULD for validators), and the gap is raised in generators/SPEC-ISSUES.md (K-I5).

producer-keys.quote: The Key, `k` field value MUST NOT be empty.
producer-keys.inference: The sentence defines the key list's value; no validator-facing sentence names an empty one. That a validator should not accept an establishment event with an empty key list is inferred and graded SHOULD (docs/design.md, Principles: an obligation the specification states only for producers is graded SHOULD for validators), and the gap is raised in generators/SPEC-ISSUES.md (K-I5).

producer-backer-unique.quote: A given AID MUST NOT appear more than once in any Backer list.
producer-backer-unique.inference: The sentence constrains a backer list's value; no validator-facing sentence names a repeated backer. That a validator should not accept an event whose backer list repeats an AID is inferred and graded SHOULD (docs/design.md, Principles: an obligation the specification states only for producers is graded SHOULD for validators), and the gap is raised in generators/SPEC-ISSUES.md (K-I5).

producer-witness.quote: When the Backers are Witnesses, then the AIDs themselves MUST be non-transferable, fully qualified public keys.
producer-witness.inference: The sentence constrains the witness AIDs a controller designates, as line 1252 ("Witnesses MUST use only nontransferable identifiers") constrains the witnesses; neither names a validator. That a validator should not accept an event designating a witness with a transferable prefix is inferred and graded SHOULD (docs/design.md, Principles: an obligation the specification states only for producers is graded SHOULD for validators), and the gap is raised in generators/SPEC-ISSUES.md (K-I5).

unsigned-may.quote: A Validator MAY drop any provided key event message body that does not have at least one attached signature from the current controlling key state of the AID of the associated [[ref: KEL]].
unsigned-may.why: Line 541 makes dropping an unsigned key event a MAY; line 1266 makes it a MUST. The cases follow line 1266, the later and more specific sentence.

receipt-drop.quote: A [[ref: Validator]] that receives a key event or non-key-event message that does not have attached at least one verifiable Controller signature MUST drop that message (i.e., not escrow or otherwise accept it).
receipt-drop.why: A receipt is a non-key-event message that carries witness signatures, not controller signatures, so read literally this sentence requires every witness receipt to be dropped. That contradicts the same paragraph's completion of a threshold 'to a receipt of that event' and lines 1286 and 1782. The cases apply the drop rule to key events only.
